questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Metals react with acids and produce metal salts and hydrogen gas.
Non-metals react with oxygen to produce non- metallic oxides which are basic in nature.
On burning, metals react with oxygen to produce metal oxides which are acidic in nature.
Less reactive metals displace more reactive metals from their compounds in aqueous solutions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metals react with acids and produce metal salts and hydrogen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an acid reacts with metal, salt and hydrogen are produced:
 
 
• Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen
 
• An example: Nitric acid + Calcium → Nitrate + Hydrogen.
 
• The salt that is produced depends upon which acid and which metal react.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Metals readily react with acid and produce hydrogen gas which burns with a pop sound.
 
• Metals are placed above hydrogen in reactivity series and displace during a reaction with an acid.
 
• As acids have a property of giving H+ ions.
 
• A resultant is formed with the release of hydrogen gas. 
 
• It doesn't matter which metal or which acid is used if there is a reaction we always get hydrogen gas as well as salt.
 
• However, how quickly the reaction goes depends on the metal used and how high up in the reactivity series it is.

questions.question: What is a biotechnological process accomplished by yeast, some type of bacteria, or some other microorganism to convert sugar into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alcoholic fermentation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alcoholic fermentation** is a complex biochemical process during which **yeasts convert sugars to ethanol, carbon dioxide, and other metabolic byproducts that contribute to the chemical composition and sensorial properties of the fermented foodstuffs**.
 
• Alcoholic fermentation is the process of using yeast to convert sugars into alcohol.
 
• The main purpose of alcohol fermentation is **to produce ATP, the energy currency for cells, under anaerobic conditions**. 
 
• So from the yeast's perspective, carbon dioxide and ethanol are waste products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9551d7d80f6f7ad4c1cd65f0e77aeea7d9215f1ca473ac115af87b50b5e4e5ee.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pasteurisation** is a process in which packaged and non-packaged foods are treated with mild heat, usually to** less than 100 °C, **to **eliminate pathogens and extend shelf life.** 
 
• **Lactic acid fermentation** is a metabolic process by which glucose or other six-carbon sugars are converted into **cellular energy and the metabolite lactate**, which is the lactic acid in solution.
 
• Glycolysis is **a cytoplasmic pathway that breaks down glucose into two three-carbon compounds and generates energy**.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques can be used to separate the impurities in Milk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Column chromatography**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Column Chromatography**

 
 
• The **separation and purification of substances from a solution to obtain the simpler substances from the complex elements is called column chromatography**.
 
• The process of separation employs **five different types of column chromatography**.
 
• The** two phases** of the procedure are the **mobile phase and the stationary phase**. 
 
• In this **solid-liquid method**, the **stationary phase is a solid** and the **mobile phase is a liquid or gas**.
 
• Applications of **Column Chromatography**
 
 
• **separation of** a complex mixture.
 
• **purification** or the process of** removing impurities**.
 
• isolation of the **active elements**.
 
• **removing metabolites **from bodily fluids.
 
• **estimation **of pharmaceutical compounds or crude extracts.
 
• Column Chromatography can also be used to **separate the impurities in Milk**.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microscopy**

 
 
• The** method of viewing things that are invisible to the naked eye is called microscopy**.
 
• ​The **range** can be any value between** mm and nm**.
 
• **Optical microscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and electron microscopy **are the three main microscopic techniques that are used.
 
 
 
• **Microtomy**
 
 
• **Microtomy **is a technique that can be used instead of electropolishing and ion milling **to prepare thin sections for materials like bones, minerals, and teeth**.
 
• The **section thickness of a microtome** can be adjusted to be between** 50 nm and 100 m, thin enough to divide a human hair across its breadth**.
 
 
 
• **Autoclave**
 
 
• An **autoclave is a device used to perform industrial and scientific procedures **that demand for **higher pressure and/or temperature** than ambient conditions.
 
• To **eliminate dangerous germs, viruses, fungus, and spores on objects inside a pressure vessel, steam is used under pressure in this machine**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of nitrate ion (NO₃^-), chloride ion (CI⁻), bromide ion (Br⁻) and iodide ion (I⁻) as per their basic strength?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is NO3- > Cl- > Br- > I-.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-), and iodide (I-) ions are all halide ions and belong to the same group in the periodic table (Group 17, the Halogens).
 
• As you move down the group, atoms will increase in size and contain more electron shells, causing the valence (outermost) electrons to be less tightly held due to an increase in the shielding effect and a larger atomic radius, which leads to these ions being less attracted to hydrogen ions (H⁺), hence less basic.
 
• On the other hand, the nitrate ion (NO₃⁻) is less atomically extensive and is what we call a** "hard ion" due to its smaller size and higher charge density.**
 
• It features oxygen, which is more electronegative. The nitrate ion is also stabilized by resonance – the ability of the negative charge to be delocalized over several atoms reduces the reactivity of the ion (in terms of accepting a proton).
 
• **However, because of the smaller size, hard ions tend to form stronger bonds with H+ ions, so they are better bases than large, soft ions.**
 
• Therefore, even though NO₃⁻ is a stable ion due to resonance, it is still harder and smaller compared with the larger halide ions, making it more basic. Hence the order of basicity, from strongest to weakest, is: NO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > Br⁻ > I⁻.

questions.question: Due to which of the following reactions are household bleaching agents using phosphorous, sulphur and chlorine formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Disproportionation reaction.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disproportionation reactions are the reason behind household bleaching agents using phosphorous, sulfur, and chlorine formed.**
 
• **Disproportionation reaction**:
 
 
• A disproportionation reaction is a specific type of redox reaction in which a species is simultaneously reduced and oxidized to form two different products.
 
• Electronic configuration of Cl is 1s²,2s²,2p⁶,3s²,3p⁵
 
• It can exhibit a maximum oxidation state of +7.
 
• In the given question, all three species can exhibit a Disproportionation reaction which simultaneously oxidizes as well as reduce.
 
• ClO - cannot undergo oxidation as +7 is the maximum oxidation state exhibited by Chlorine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A displacement reaction:**

 
 
• It is a type of reaction in which part of one reactant is replaced by another reactant.
 
• There are two types of displacement reactions.
 
 
• **Single displacement reactions**: These are those reactions in which one reactant replaces part of the other. Eg: Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu.
 
• **Double displacement reactions:** These are those reactions in which the cations and anions in the reactants switch partners to form products. Eg: AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3.
 
 
 
• A displacement reaction is also known as a** replacement reaction or a metathesis reaction.**
 
 
 
• **Combination reaction:**
 
 
• A combination reaction also termed a synthesis reaction is about two or more reactants or substances combining with each other to form a new product.
 
• Rust, which is a result of a combination reaction of oxygen and iron could serve as one of the examples of a combination reaction.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition reaction:**
 
 
• Those reactions in which a compound splits up into two or simpler substances are known as decomposition reactions.
 
• A decomposition reaction is the opposite of a combination reaction.
 
 
• **Thermal decomposition:**
 
 
• When a decomposition reaction is carried out by heating, it is called thermal decomposition. The decomposition reaction of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide is an example of thermal decomposition. Example: 2FeSO4 - Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3.

questions.question: Which element in the modern periodic table has the same number of valence electrons as that of caesium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** is the correct answer because it shares the **same number of valence electrons as Caesium.**
 
• Both Potassium (K) and Caesium (Cs) belong to** Group 1 of the Periodic **Table, also known as **alkali metals.**
 
• Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have the same number of valence electrons - in this case, **one.**
 
• The number of **valence electrons remains constant** when moving vertically down a group in the Periodic Table.
 
• Valence electrons are crucial as they determine how an atom will bond with other atoms. **Both K and Cs, being alkali metals,** are highly reactive and tend to donate their one valence electron during chemical reactions.
 
• This is why the characteristics and chemical behaviour of K and Cs are quite similar. They both form +1 ions and have similar properties owing to the **same valence electron.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminium:**

 
 
• **Aluminium (Al) **belongs to **Group 13** of the Periodic Table.
 
• It has three valence electrons, which affects its** reactivity and oxidation states.**
 
• In chemical reactions, Aluminium often loses these electrons, resulting in a **+3 ion**, unlike Cs and K which forms **+1 ions.**
 
• Despite its difference in reactivity from Cs and K, Aluminium is widely used due to its **lightweight and resistance to corrosion.**
 
 
 
• **Barium:**
 
 
• **Barium (Ba)** is part of **Group 2**, also known as the **alkaline earth metals.**
 
• Unlike Cs and K which have a single valence electron, Barium has** two valence electrons.**
 
• This difference in the number of valence electrons makes it form **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Barium compounds show a unique property in that they are very heavy, making them useful for **blocking X-ray and radiation emission**, as in Barium meal used in **radiography.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium:**
 
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** is also a member of **Group 2**, just like Barium.
 
• It has two valence electrons and hence, forms **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Its chemical behaviour, influenced by the number of valence electrons, is thus distinct from Cs and K.
 
• Calcium is crucial for human health, particularly for the development and maintenance of bones. It's also an important component of the earth's crust; compounds such as calcium carbonate are found in rocks like limestone and marble.

questions.question: In 1937, who along with Sir Christopher Ingold, proposed nucleophilic substitution reactions of alkyl halides and related compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Edward Davies Hughes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Christopher Ingold **

 
 
• He was a British chemist who made significant contributions to the field of organic chemistry.
 
 
 
• Alkyl halides are organic compounds that contain a halogen atom (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, or iodine) bonded to an alkyl group (a group of carbon and hydrogen atoms).
 
• The process of nucleophilic substitution involves the replacement of a halogen atom in an alkyl halide with a nucleophile (an electron-rich species).
 
• **Edward Davies Hughes:-**
 
 
• **​**He was a Welsh chemist who is known for his work on the synthesis of organic compounds and the study of nucleophilic substitution reactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sergei Winogradsky:-**

 
 
• He was a Russian microbiologist who is known for his work on the nitrogen cycle and the discovery of lithotrophs (organisms that can metabolize inorganic compounds).
 
 
 
• **Jacobus Hendricus:-**
 
 
• He was a Dutch chemist who is known for his work on the structure and properties of organic compounds, particularly carbohydrates.
 
 
 
• **Victor Grignard:-**
 
 
• He was a French chemist who is known for his work on organometallic compounds and the development of the Grignard reagent (a reagent used in organic synthesis).

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid bond in Alkenes that connects carbon atoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double bond.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Alkenes:-**

 
 
• **These are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond. **
 
• The general formula for alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ, where n is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.
 
• **The carbon-carbon double bond in alkenes is formed by the overlap of one sigma bond and one pi bond. **
 
• The sigma bond is formed by the overlap of two hybridized sp2 orbitals from each carbon atom.
 
• **The pi bond is formed by the overlap of two unhybridized p orbitals from each carbon atom.**
 
• The pi bond is weaker than the sigma bond, and this makes alkenes more reactive than alkanes, which only contain single bonds between carbon atoms.

questions.question: Which among the following alloys is made up of copper and zinc?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dutch Metal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dutch Metal, **also known as **Dutch gold or composition gold, is an alloy primarily composed of copper and zinc.**
 
• It's an alloy of** approximately 85% copper and 15% zinc.**
 
• Despite its name, **Dutch Metal doesn't contain gold.**
 
• It's often used because of its **gold-like appearance in applications such as gilding and jewellery.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monel Metal:**

 
 
• **​**This is an alloy primarily **composed of nickel and copper.**
 
• It's highly resistant to corrosion and acids, **and it's used in various applications, such as marine and chemical environments.**
 
 
 
• **Magnalium:**
 
 
• **​**It's an aluminium alloy that's mixed with** 1.5% to 2% magnesium.**
 
• It's lighter than aluminium and is often used in applications where lightweight strength is needed, such as in the construction of aircraft.
 
 
 
• **Rolled Gold:**
 
 
• **Also known as gold-filled,** it's a** hybrid material composed of a thin layer of gold that's bonded to a base of either silver or a base metal. It's primarily used in jewellery.**

questions.question: Which is the toxin-causing bacterium that spoils cream, cheese and milk and makes them taste bitter, sour or bitter?

__
 
• The **bacterium Bacillus cereus** causes **spoilage of cream, cheese and milk** and makes them taste rancid, sour or bitter.
 
• **Bacillus cereus is a ****Gram-positive****, ****rod-shaped, facultatively anaerobic, motile, beta-hemolytic, spore-forming bacterium commonly found in soil, food and marine sponges**. 
 
• The specific name,** cereus, meaning "waxy" in Latin,** refers to the appearance of colonies grown on **blood agar.**
 
• Bacillus cereus is a foodborne pathogen that **can produce toxins, causing two types of gastrointestinal illness: the emetic (vomiting) syndrome and the diarrhoeal syndrome**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a technique or a step to convert normal water to potable water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bromination: It is not used as a technique to convert normal water to potable water.
 
• While bromine can be used as a disinfectant, it is generally employed in specific industrial or specialized applications, such as swimming pools, spas, or certain water treatment processes.
 
• Bromine's usage for general potable water treatment is not as prevalent as chlorine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Filtration: Filtration is a common technique used to remove solid particles, sediments, and larger contaminants from water. It involves passing the water through a filtration medium or membrane that traps impurities and allows clean water to pass through.
 
• Boiling: Boiling water is an effective method to kill most types of pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When water is brought to a rolling boil for a certain duration (usually around one minute), it helps in rendering the water safe for consumption by destroying harmful microorganisms.
 
• Chlorination: Chlorination is a widely used method for disinfecting and purifying water. It involves adding a small amount of chlorine, usually in the form of chlorine gas or chlorine compounds like sodium hypochlorite or calcium hypochlorite, to the water. Chlorine acts as a disinfectant, killing bacteria, viruses, and other harmful microorganisms, thus making the water safe to drink.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Living organisms can survive a wide range of pH change.

• pH scale was discovered by Soren Sorensen.
 
• The range of pH scale 0 to 14.

• If pH = 7 then solution is neutral
 
 
 
• The strength of acids and bases depends on the number of H+ ions and OH- ions produced, respectively.
 
• When the pH of rainwater is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain.
 
• The pH value of the Milk of Magnesia is 10.5.

questions.question: What is the atomic mass of sodium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The atomic mass of an element represents the average mass of an atom of that element, taking into account the different isotopes and their relative abundances.
 
• Sodium is a chemical element with the symbol Na and atomic number 11. It belongs to the alkali metal group on the periodic table.
 
• The atomic mass of sodium is approximately 22.99 atomic mass units (AMU).
 
• The atomic mass of an element is calculated by summing the masses of its isotopes, multiplied by their respective abundances, and expressed in atomic mass units.
 
• Sodium has two stable isotopes: sodium-23 (Na-23) and sodium-22 (Na-22).
 
• The most abundant isotope of sodium is sodium-23, which accounts for approximately 100% of natural sodium. It has an atomic mass of 22.98976928 amu.
 
• Sodium-22 is a less abundant isotope and has an atomic mass of 21.994437 amu.
 
• The atomic mass listed on the periodic table for sodium (22.99 amu) is a weighted average of the masses of its isotopes, considering their natural abundance.
 
• The atomic mass of an element may be slightly different from the mass number of its most abundant isotope due to the presence of other isotopes and their relative abundances.
 
• The atomic mass of sodium is important in various scientific fields, such as chemistry and physics, as it is used in stoichiometric calculations, determining molar mass, and understanding the behavior of sodium in chemical reactions.

questions.question: Which chemical reaction takes place during the cooking of meat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Maillard reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Maillard reaction**__

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned food its distinctive flavour.
 
• Like caramelization, it is a form of non-enzymatic browning.
 
• **It takes place during the cooking of meat**.
 
• The reactive carbonyl group of the sugar interacts with the nucleophilic amino group of the amino acid, and interesting but poorly characterized odour and flavour molecules result.
 
 
 
• ** The Gattermann reaction**
 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which aromatic compounds are formulated by a mixture of hydrogen cyanide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst.
 
 
 
• **The Swartz reaction**
 
 
• It is a reaction in which alkyl fluoride are formed when alkyl bromide or chloride reacts with metal fluorides.
 
 
 
• **The Finkelstein reaction**
 
 
• It is a preparation of alkyl iodide from alkyl bromide or chloride with potassium or sodium iodide in acetone.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions leads to the formation of glucose pentaacetate from acetic anhydride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetylation of glucose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acetylation of glucose** refers to the chemical reaction where glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate.
 
• In this reaction, the hydroxyl groups (-OH) of glucose are replaced by acetyl groups (-COCH₃).
 
• The process results in the formation of **glucose pentaacetate**, which is a derivative of glucose where all five hydroxyl groups are acetylated.
 
• This reaction is an example of an **esterification** reaction, specifically known as acetylation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose pentaacetate** is an important compound in organic chemistry and biochemistry, often used in research and industry.
 
• The reaction can be represented by the equation:

 **Glucose + Acetic Anhydride → Glucose Pentaacetate + Acetic Acid**
 
• This reaction is typically carried out in the presence of a catalyst such as pyridine to facilitate the acetylation process.
 
• Acetylation is a common method used to protect hydroxyl groups during chemical synthesis.

questions.question: What kind of smell do Esters have?

The correct answer is __**Sweet smells like fruits.**__

__
 
• **Esters:-**

 
 
• **They have a sweet smell like fruits. This is because they are commonly found in fruits and are responsible for their characteristic aroma.**
 
• Esters are organic compounds that are formed from the reaction between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rotten egg smell:-**

 
 
• It is typically associated with hydrogen sulfide gas, which is produced when organic matter decomposes in the absence of oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Floral smell:-**
 
 
• It is associated with various compounds found in flowers, such as essential oils and terpenes.
 
 
 
• **Pungent smell:-**
 
 
• It is a general term used to describe strong and unpleasant odors, which can be caused by a wide range of compounds, including sulfur compounds, ammonia, and certain volatile organic compounds.

questions.question: The method of separating a mixture of soluble solids by dissolving them in a suitable hot solvent and then lowering the temperature slowly is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fractional crystallisation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fractional crystallisation** is a method of separating a mixture of soluble solids.
 
• This process involves dissolving the mixture in a suitable hot solvent.
 
• The temperature is then slowly lowered, which causes the different components to crystallise at different temperatures.
 
• This method is used to purify substances and separate components based on their solubility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation** is a process where a solid changes directly into a gas without going through a liquid phase.
 
• **Azeotropic distillation** is used to separate components of a mixture by distillation, involving an azeotrope.
 
• **Dephlegmation** is a process used in the distillation of mixtures to separate components with close boiling points.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about compounds ?

options.text: The constituents can be separated only by chemical or electrochemical reactions.
The composition of each new substance is always ﬁxed.
Elements react to form new compounds.

questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is __**Compounds have a variable composition**__.

__
 
• Compounds have a **fixed composition** throughout the mass, Hence** Option 2 is Not true.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Properties of Compound**

 
 
• A compound is a substance made up of two or more elements chemically combined in a **fixed proportion by mass**.
 
• A compound **cannot **be separated into its constituents by physical processes (It can only be separated into

 its constituents by chemical processes).
 
• The properties of a compound are entirely different from those of its constituents.
 
• Energy (in the form of heat, light, etc.) is usually given out or absorbed during the preparation of a compound.
 
• The composition of a compound is fixed, the constituents are present in a fixed proportion by mass.
 
• A compound has a definite formula.
 
• A compound has a fixed melting point, boiling point.

questions.question: Which fibre among the following is used to make rayon clothing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

__
 
• **​Rayon is a man-made fiber prepared by chemical treatment from a natural raw material called cellulose**__.

 __
 
• The cellulose needed to make rayon is obtained from wood pulp. Rayon is obtained by chemical treatment of wood pulp.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pectin **is a fiber found in fruits.

 
 
• It is often used as a thickener in cooking and baking.
 
• It is also sometimes used to make medicine.
 
• People use pectin for **high cholesterol, high triglycerides, heartburn**, and many other conditions, but there is no good scientific evidence to support these uses.
 
 
 
• **Mucilage **is a thick, sticky substance produced by almost all plants and some microorganisms.
 
 
• These microorganisms include protists which use it for their movement.
 
• The direction of their movement is always opposite to that of the mucous secretion.
 
• It is a polar glycoprotein and an exopolysaccharide. In plants, mucilage plays a role in water and food storage, seed germination and membrane thickening.
 
• **Cacti **(and other succulents) and flaxseeds are especially rich sources of mucilage.
 
 
 
• **Gum **base is made of polymers, plasticizers, and resins. Polymers, including elastomers, are responsible for the stretchy and sticky nature of chewing gum.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Salts of a strong acid and weak base are acidic with pH value less than 7.

II. When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (called brine), it decomposes to form sodium oxide.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Only I**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pH value of salts of strong acid and strong base is 7__.

 __
 
• The salts are from a strong acid and strong base that do not hydrolyze and the resulting salt pH will remain 7.
 
• The anion in the salt form's strong base does not attract the H+ from the water.
 
 
 
• Salt of a strong acid and a weak base is acidic with a pH value less than 7 because acid is strong which retains the pH value less than 7. ***Statement I is correct__***
 
• Salt of a weak acid and strong base is base with a pH value of more than 7 because the base is strong hence pH of the whole solution will be more than 7.
 
• Salt of a strong acid and strong base is neutral because both are strong and cancels strong effects of each other, the pH will be 7.

Statement II:(Incorrect)

 
• When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of **sodium Chloride (brine),** it decomposes to form **NaOH + H₂ + CI₂.**
 
• **Brine** is a saturated solution of **NaCl (Sodium chloride).**
 
• Electrolytic decomposition of solution gives** Cl₂ (Chlorine)** at the **anode **and **H₂ (Hydrogen)** is formed at the** cathode and NaOH (Sodium hydroxide )** is formed near to the cathode.
 
• This process is known as **chor- alkali process.**
